parsed.explanation: A visibly transgender visitor faces arbitrary capture in mass raids under the post-March 2022 exception regime, birth-sex prison placement, forcible hair-shaving, handcuffed punishment drills, sexual assault and denial of HIV care, with one woman held about four months before a judge found the arrest unsupported while another remained imprisoned. Societal hostility is extreme, with 85% in a 2013 study deeming attacks on transgender people acceptable, police historically refusing cooperation, and gangs targeting LGBT people. A 2020 conviction of three police officers for killing a transgender woman and hate-crime penalties are documented mitigations, but they do not remedy the ongoing custody regime or thin recourse.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans women arbitrarily captured in mass raids since March 2022 are held in ordinary prisons without gender-identity accommodation; documented abuse includes forcible hair shaving, handcuffed outdoor punishment drills in the sun, denial of HIV clinic access, searches, theft and sexual assault by police, soldiers and guards.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A judge freed one detained trans woman after about four months, finding the arrest unsupported; three police officers were convicted in 2020 and sentenced to 20 years each for killing a transgender woman.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest leads from police lockup to prison custody where birth-sex placement and effeminate-behaviour bans expose detainees to targeted punishment and assault; release required judicial intervention after months.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Prison rules strictly forbid effeminate dress or behaviour; hospital patients report longer waits and denial of care, with specialists dismissing problems as side effects of being transgender.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 2009 health-ministry guidelines and HIV/AIDS plan prohibit sexual-orientation discrimination in health services.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Paper non-discrimination guidance coexists with documented custodial and hospital practices that override it in placement and treatment.

care_services.exposure: Hormone therapy and surgery access is severely restricted by lack of protocols; trans women report not seeking help after surgical side effects due to distrust, and a detainee was denied HIV clinic access.
care_services.protection: 2009 guidelines ban discrimination against LGBT and HIV-positive people in health services.
care_services.interaction: Care denial is compounded in custody, where clinic access can be withheld as punishment and no accommodation is provided.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Exception-regime mass raids arbitrarily capture trans women; police have shown blatant refusal to cooperate in LGBT death investigations, and international reports document failure to address violence and entrenched discrimination.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-crime framework since 2015 provides 30-60 years for bias-motivated killing and 3-6 years for sexual-orientation/gender-identity hate crimes; one police homicide conviction resulted in 20-year sentences.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Formal hate-crime penalties contrast with operational police refusal and custodial abuse; the single documented conviction does not show a working system for routine raids or assaults.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Gang violence includes physical and sexual assault, forced recruitment and extortion targeting LGBT people; 2013 study found 85% considered attacking a transgender person acceptable and 62% did not accept homosexuality.
street_violence_police_response.protection: The 2020 homicide prosecution and conviction of three police officers shows attackers can be punished, hailed as a pivotal advance.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Societal acceptance of attacks plus police non-cooperation undermines the deterrent value of the isolated conviction, especially outside the capital case.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: International bodies document obstacles to protection; a second detained trans woman remained imprisoned after the first was freed, and whether further hate-crime convictions occurred is not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Judicial release after unsupported arrest and the 2020 police-murder conviction demonstrate courts can impose consequences in some cases.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are episodic and slow relative to months-long detention, leaving no documented timely remedy for custody abuse or care denial.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar to 0.25-C: birth-sex prison housing, frequent assaults, slow remedies and no documented capital pathway. This case is at or slightly below because state actors are documented committing sexual assault and soldiers/police participate, and arbitrary mass-raid detention lasted months.

Lower than 0.35-B: that anchor involves hours-long stops, confiscation and fines without imprisonment. Here documented exposure escalates to months of prison, forced punishment drills and sexual assault, a materially more severe tier.

Much lower than 0.65-A: that anchor has national equality protection, brief detention, release, apology and compensation. Here protection failed for months, abuse was custodial and state-linked, and no comparable compensation or discipline is documented.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is dominated by the exception-regime custody pipeline: arbitrary raids can place a transgender visitor in birth-sex prisons where effeminate presentation itself triggers searches, punishment, sexual assault and care denial. Hate-crime statutes and one landmark conviction of police killers are real but narrow mitigations; they have not prevented ongoing raids, police non-cooperation, or extreme social license for attacks. No border-document exposure, execution pathway, or minor-specific rule is documented. Severity after outing is therefore carceral and abusive rather than merely exclusionary, placing the jurisdiction near the 0.25 tier.
